title: A Gis-Based Decision Support Model (DSM) for Harvesting System Selection on Steep Terrain: Integrating Operational and Silvicultural Criteria
content: The objective of this study is to create a GIS-based decision support model for steep terrain timber harvesting. The tool integrates multiple raster layers, each representing a critical aspect of mechanized timber harvesting, and uses them to generate a composite map that aids in decision-making about suitable areas for specific machine configurations. The innovation lies in two pivotal aspects: first, the tool integrates silvicultural considerations alongside operational criteria; second, it employs a new methodology that factors in these silvicultural criteria without depending on resource-intensive point cloud data. Instead, the methodology integrates aerial imagery in the form of an orthofoto, and the deep-learning algorithm DeepForest for the evaluation of forest stand characteristics. The procedure was tested in South Tyrol, Italy, using remotely sensed data and validated against ground-based inventory data. While the results indicate an underestimation of stem numbers and a tendency to underrate small tree dimensions, overall performance statistics are promising. This makes the procedure a valuable tool for forest management planning, effectively integrating operational and silvicultural considerations.
